purpose: Ancient physical anchor for testing sign/phonetic mapping, rather than a modern Latin word list.
target: OIM A2480, Chicago Syllabary, object60 in ISAC OIMP32 Visible Language
selection: First specific institutional object returned by the current primary-source search for ancient syllabaries. Not selected by resemblance to a Kazakh word.
prior: Modern catalogue description already exposed: first-millennium object, eight columns arranged as two sets of four, traditional interpretation of pronunciation/sign/name/Akkadian. These roles are claims to test, not raw observations; no blind claim.
questions: Is a real photograph included and is its source distinct from a modern drawing?
Can repeated graph groups and row alignment be resolved without assigning Latin sound values?
Does any one-to-many graphic pairing become visible, and what competing explanations remain?
gate: Need distinct wedge groups and at least two aligned rows for local graphic pairing. Otherwise retain unresolved and no phonetic result.
scope: Inspect physical-photo publication and preserve exact page/crop provenance. Do not project first-millennium readings directly onto third/fourth-millennium tablets.
